questions.scenario: You are bored in class and start doodling in the back of your notebook. What are you most likely drawing?

options.text: Detailed, imaginative characters, cool armor, or fantasy landscapes.
A tiny flipbook in the corner of the pages to make a stick figure run.
A short comic strip with panels, speech bubbles, and a funny punchline.
Shading a 3D object to make it pop off the page, or drawing explosions.

questions.scenario: You are watching a huge Marvel-style blockbuster movie. What makes you say 'Wow!'?

options.text: The incredible costume designs and the beautiful alien worlds.
How fluidly the CGI characters fight, jump, and express emotion.
The epic camera angles and how perfectly the scenes flow together.
Trying to figure out how they blended real actors with giant CGI explosions.

questions.scenario: Your group has to present a project in front of the class. What is your role?

options.text: Designing the slides so they look aesthetically pleasing and colorful.
Adding cool transitions, GIFs, and moving text to keep the audience awake.
Structuring the script so the presentation has a great beginning, middle, and end.
Handling the tech—making sure the audio, videos, and lighting work perfectly.

questions.scenario: You are playing a new video game. What is your favorite thing to do?

options.text: Taking screenshots using 'Photo Mode' because the environments are gorgeous.
Enjoying the snappy, satisfying way your character runs and attacks.
Paying deep attention to the cinematic cutscenes and the game's lore.
Noticing the realistic water ripples, fire particles, and lighting effects.

questions.scenario: If you had a magic power related to art, what would it be?

options.text: The ability to instantly paint anything exactly as I imagine it in my head.
The ability to touch a drawing and make it literally come alive and walk around.
The ability to pause, rewind, or change camera angles in real life like a movie director.
The ability to shoot realistic fireballs, sparkles, or lightning from my hands.

questions.scenario: You are uploading a post or making a Reel/TikTok. What is your focus?

options.text: Making sure the color palette and overall 'vibe' of the photo is flawless.
Creating a stop-motion video or syncing my movements perfectly to the beat.
Making sure the video tells a mini-story with a good setup and punchline.
Using heavy editing, green screens, and crazy filters to trick the viewer.

questions.scenario: A friend tells you a really funny story about something that happened to them. How does your brain process it?

options.text: I immediately picture exactly what the setting and the people looked like.
I focus on their body language and facial expressions as they tell the story.
I imagine the story playing out in my head like a series of comic book panels.
I imagine editing their story into a video with funny sound effects and zoom-ins.

questions.scenario: You are given a random object on your desk, like a stapler. What do you do with it?

options.text: I look at its shape and imagine it as a futuristic spaceship.
I make it 'walk' across the desk and give it a funny voice.
I plan a mini-movie where the stapler has an epic battle with a pencil.
I take a picture of it and imagine photoshopping laser beams coming out of it.

questions.scenario: What kind of YouTube video are you most likely to watch late at night?

options.text: A speed-painting video showing an artist creating a masterpiece from scratch.
A video breaking down the principles of animation or cartoon reactions.
A video essay analyzing why a specific movie scene is an absolute masterpiece.
A 'behind-the-scenes' video showing how movies created fake CGI monsters.

questions.scenario: What is the best compliment someone could give you about your work?

options.text: 'Your art style is so unique and visually stunning!'
'The way that character moves feels so incredibly alive and natural!'
'I was on the edge of my seat! The pacing of your story is perfect.'
'That edit looked so real, I honestly thought it was actual magic.'

Concept_Artist.title: Concept Artist / Illustrator
Concept_Artist.primary_match_text: You are the ultimate visionary. You love dreaming up new worlds, focusing on aesthetics, and bringing ideas from your imagination into visual reality.
Concept_Artist.day_in_the_life: Drawing the very first sketches of characters, environments, and props for movies or video games before anyone else starts working on them.
Concept_Artist.alternative_match_text: Since you have a great eye for detail and design, working as an illustrator for books or comics is also a fantastic backup plan.
Concept_Artist.roadmap: Take Any Stream (Fine Arts/Humanities preferred) in 11th/12th. Pursue a BFA (Bachelor of Fine Arts) in Illustration, Digital Art, or Concept Design. Build a strong digital portfolio.

Animator.title: 2D/3D Animator
Animator.primary_match_text: You are fascinated by movement and life. You have the patience to tweak tiny details and love making static things breathe, jump, and express emotion.
Animator.day_in_the_life: Using software to pose 3D models or drawing 2D frames to create running cycles, lip-syncing dialogue, and intense action sequences for films or games.
Animator.alternative_match_text: Because you understand movement and timing so well, motion graphics (creating animated text and logos for brands) is a great alternative.
Animator.roadmap: Take Any Stream in 11th/12th. Pursue a B.Sc or B.Des in Animation and Multimedia. Master software like Maya, Blender, or Toon Boom Harmony.

Storyboard_Artist.title: Storyboard Artist
Storyboard_Artist.primary_match_text: You are a visual director. You think in sequences, love planning out stories, and have a natural sense of camera angles, pacing, and cinematic flow.
Storyboard_Artist.day_in_the_life: Reading a script and sketching out comic-book-like panels to show the director exactly how the movie, ad, or animation should look shot-by-shot.
Storyboard_Artist.alternative_match_text: With your strong grasp of pacing and narrative, you could also easily transition into Film Directing or Comic Book Creation.
Storyboard_Artist.roadmap: Take Any Stream in 11th/12th. Pursue a degree in Animation, Film Making, or Sequential Art. Practice visual storytelling and film cinematography rules.

VFX_Artist.title: VFX & Compositing Artist
VFX_Artist.primary_match_text: You are the digital wizard. You love blending the real world with the impossible, solving technical puzzles, and making digital illusions look 100% real.
VFX_Artist.day_in_the_life: Adding CGI monsters into live-action footage, creating realistic explosions, simulating water physics, or removing green screens for blockbuster movies.
VFX_Artist.alternative_match_text: Since you are great at mixing elements and technical problem-solving, working as a Video Editor or Technical Director (TD) is a solid backup.
VFX_Artist.roadmap: Take Science (PCM) or Commerce with Computers in 11th/12th for a technical edge. Pursue a B.Sc in VFX, Animation, or Computer Graphics. Master software like Nuke, After Effects, or Houdini.
